agree.reason: The candid handling of the GMP gap and the concrete safety record could earn a phone screen from a skeptical HR manager, but the letter shows no knowledge of how a plant actually works (SOPs, deviations, qualification), so it may not change her assumption about teachers.

honest.reason: It wisely drops the unsupported 'cut training time in half' claim, but 'shortening training without weakening it is what I've spent nine years doing' has no support in the brief, and 'commit to this move' and the new teachers supervising alone are added details.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are restated rather than worked: it doesn't give the 17-point (about 41% relative) pass-rate rise, the roughly 1,000 student-years without a serious injury, or the roughly 18 teachers trained over nine years.

right_comparison.reason: It implicitly sets itself against a candidate who already has GMP experience and argues the safety-program work is close to it, but it never describes the plant's current training baseline or what that comparison actually looks like.

qualification.reason: The plans to learn the quality team's documentation 'in my first weeks' and to measure sign-off time have no date, target number, or stated consequence the reader could check.

objections.reason: It meets the main objection (no regulated-industry, GMP, or LMS experience) directly and offers a credible plan, though the bridge to GMP stays general.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted one-page cover letter of appropriate length.
